The [[Canadian province]] of [[Nova Scotia]] was a [[British colony]] with a system of [[responsible government]] since 1848, before it joined [[Canadian Confederation]] in 1867. Since Confederation, the province has been a part of the Canadian [[federation]] and has kept its own legislature to deal with provincial matters.<ref name=history />

Nova Scotia has a unicameral [[Westminster-style]] [[parliamentary government]], in which the premier is the leader of the party that controls the most seats in the [[Nova Scotia House of Assembly|House of Assembly]].  The premier is Nova Scotia's [[head of government]], and the [[Monarchy in Nova Scotia|king in right of Nova Scotia]] is its [[head of state]] and is represented by the [[lieutenant governor of Nova Scotia]]. The premier picks a cabinet from the elected members to form the [[Executive Council of Nova Scotia]], and presides over that body.<ref name=history>{{cite web|access-date=November 11, 2008 |url=http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/confederation/023001-2125-e.html |date=May 2, 2005 |title=Nova Scotia |publisher=Library and Archives Canada |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080801075902/http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/confederation/023001-2125-e.html |archive-date=August 1, 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Members are first elected to the House during [[List of Nova Scotia general elections (post-Confederation)|general elections]]. General elections must be conducted every five years from the date of the last election, but the premier may ask for early [[Dissolution of parliament#Canada|dissolution]] of the Legislative Assembly. An election may also occur if the governing party loses the confidence of the legislature by the defeat of a supply bill or tabling of a confidence motion.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=November 11, 2008|url=http://www.parl.gc.ca/common/bills_ls.asp?lang=E&ls=c16&source=library_prb&Parl=39&Ses=1|title=Bill C-16: An Act to amend the Canada Elections Act|publisher=Parliament of Canada|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081019045510/http://www.parl.gc.ca/common/bills_ls.asp?lang=E&ls=c16&source=library_prb&Parl=39&Ses=1|archive-date=October 19, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> Nova Scotia has had 27 individuals serve as premier since Confederation, of which 12 were [[Progressive Conservative Association of Nova Scotia|Conservatives]], 14 were [[Nova Scotia Liberal Party|Liberals]], and one [[Nova Scotia New Democratic Party|New Democrat]].

Two premiers of Nova Scotia later became [[Prime Minister of Canada|prime minister of Canada]], [[John Sparrow David Thompson]] and [[Charles Tupper]].
